source.title: FDA approves imlunestrant in combination with abemaciclib for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) with abemaciclib on 18 September 2026 for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer.
The US FDA approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) with abemaciclib (Verzenio) on 18 September 2026.
It applies to adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
The FDA also approved the Guardant360 CDx test to identify ESR1 mutations.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 18 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) in combination with abemaciclib (Verzenio).
The approval is for adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
The FDA also approved the Guardant360 CDx assay as a companion diagnostic to identify breast cancers with ESR1 mutations for treatment with imlunestrant and abemaciclib.
The FDA says the approval rests on the phase 3 EMBER-3 trial, in which patients were randomly assigned to imlunestrant, standard endocrine therapy, or imlunestrant with abemaciclib.
The FDA had approved imlunestrant alone in September 2025 for ESR1-mutated disease that had progressed after at least one line of endocrine therapy.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Adds Boxed Warning to Labeling for Ferric Carboxymaltose Injection (Injectafer) to Describe Risk of Low Phosphate Levels

sentences.sentence: The US FDA said on 1 September 2026 that it added a boxed warning to Injectafer (ferric carboxymaltose) about the risk of low blood phosphate.
The US FDA added a boxed warning to Injectafer (ferric carboxymaltose) in a safety communication dated 1 September 2026.
The warning describes the risk of symptomatic hypophosphataemia, meaning low blood phosphate.
The FDA says reports continued despite earlier labelling changes in 2020 and 2023.
This is a US decision; UK availability and labelling are decided separately.
On 1 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published a drug safety communication about ferric carboxymaltose injection, marketed as Injectafer.
The FDA says it approved label revisions that add a boxed warning, its most prominent safety warning.
The warning describes the risk of symptomatic hypophosphataemia, which is low phosphate in the blood.
It recommends phosphate monitoring in patients at risk and in any patient who receives a repeat course of treatment within three months of the previous course.
The FDA says symptomatic hypophosphataemia continued to be reported despite labelling changes in February 2020 and May 2023.
It also reports that, in data from its Sentinel System, serum phosphate testing took place in fewer than 20% of administration episodes.
Ferric carboxymaltose is an iron replacement given by injection into a vein.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves First Once-Weekly Insulin for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Pediatric Patients

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved Awiqli (insulin icodec) for children aged 10 and older with type 2 diabetes, the first once-weekly insulin approved for this group.
The US FDA approved Awiqli (insulin icodec-abae) for children with type 2 diabetes.
The FDA says it is the first once-weekly insulin approved for children with type 2 diabetes.
The approval covers patients aged 10 and older and is used alongside diet and exercise.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Awiqli (insulin icodec-abae) for children aged 10 and older with type 2 diabetes.
The FDA describes it as the first once-weekly insulin approved for this group.
It is a subcutaneous injection used alongside diet and exercise.
The FDA says the approval relied on a single-dose pharmacokinetic study in 18 children and that it expects the medicine to lower blood glucose in children much as it does in adults.
Awiqli had already been approved for adults earlier in 2026.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
